experiment.handshake: full ring bridge, phase 8, ring B consumed at ~280 packets/s
experiment.result: parse_entry hits = 1, and the milestone histogram holds exactly one entry per kind (CRT entry, WinMain, ... each 1)

conclusion: the launcher removes a breakpoint after its first hit. A count of 1 therefore means 'reached at least once', never 'reached exactly once'. This invalidates my earlier 'the loop runs once' reading, but not the recv_helper count of 0, which remains reliable (a never-hit breakpoint proves the function was never entered).
implications: 0x5C2260 is entered at least once (confirmed), and likely every frame
so 0x5C2260 returns before 0x5C2380 every time, but none of the known early-exit conditions (phase<7 or readcount<4) should hold with phase 8 and a 687/1172-byte packet

or patch the early exits to call a scratch logger instead of returning
